draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Fort! The Victorian Gothic buildings on one side of the Oval Maidan here and the Art Deco row on the other side, stretching toward Marine Drive, were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site together in 2018.
draft.hungryLine: My notes don't name a place to eat in Fort, so follow the office lunch crowd and see where they queue.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Jehangir Art Gallery and the National Gallery of Modern Art are both about 8 minutes on foot, and the Keneseth Eliyahoo Synagogue is around 10 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the Oval Maidan with Gothic spires on one side and Art Deco on the other, then wander west to Marine Drive.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Dr B. R. Ambedkar studied at Elphinstone High School here from 1904 to 1907, the first person from the Dalit caste to do so.

spots.name: Jehangir Art Gallery
spots.detail: 8 min walk · Four exhibition halls at Kala Ghoda, open since 1952

spots.name: National Gallery of Modern Art
spots.detail: 8 min walk · Art collections inside the 1911 Cowasji Jehangir Hall

spots.name: Bombay High Court
spots.detail: By the Oval Maidan · One of India's oldest high courts, part of the UNESCO ensemble

tips.title: Walk the ensemble early.
tips.body: The Gothic and Art Deco buildings are best seen on foot around the Oval Maidan, before the midday heat.

tips.title: Look out to Marine Drive.
tips.body: The Art Deco side of the Oval runs to Marine Drive, where Express Towers once was the tallest building in South Asia.

story.title: Elphinstone High School
story.body: An English-medium school opened in honour of Governor Mountstuart Elphinstone. Dr B. R. Ambedkar later studied here.

story.title: Cowasji Jehangir Hall
story.body: George Wittet built the hall with funds from Cowasji Jehangir. Since 1996 it has housed the National Gallery of Modern Art.

story.title: An art gallery for the city
story.body: Sir Cowasji Jehangir built Jehangir Art Gallery at Kala Ghoda, urged on by K. K. Hebbar and Homi J. Bhabha.

story.title: Up on Marine Drive
story.body: The 25-storey Express Towers went up on Marine Drive in Nariman Point. At 105 metres it was the tallest building in South Asia for about two years.

story.title: World Heritage
story.body: UNESCO listed the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensembles of Mumbai, 94 buildings around the Oval Maidan from the High Court to Marine Drive.
